- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early/medium horizon (first 10–15 days) — apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for short-term forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes, model overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the 2–5 day window following a spike.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends — increase forecast by 1–3% during sustained declines.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day average of history is > forecast, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with historical mean.
- Model lags in responding to recent price drops — if true outcome drops below 30-day moving average, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% within 3–5 days.
- Model overreacts to minor volatility — avoid sharp upward revisions unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of higher prices.
